plain_english_policy: This bill creates a specific program for Etowah County to hire retired law enforcement officers as part-time school resource officers (SROs). The policy direction is to expand local safety resources by allowing retirees from municipal police, sheriff's departments, or other certified positions to work in schools without receiving new health insurance or retirement benefits. It grants these part-time SROs full legal powers of a peace officer and provides immunity for the hiring chiefs/sheriffs regarding civil liability. The bill also establishes a preference system where retired local officers are prioritized over sheriff's deputies within city limits, while preferring deputy sheriffs in unincorporated areas.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would authorize Etowah County schools to employ part-time SROs using existing retirees. This expands the pool of available safety personnel without creating new full-time positions or altering state-wide pay scales, as funding and wages are left to local discretion. It effectively codifies a partnership between retired law enforcement agencies and local school districts in Etowah County.
sponsorship_supports_position: Representative Ford (N & P) advanced this bill to enable part-time SRO roles for retirees specifically within Etowah County.
evidence_quotes: "to allow retired law enforcement officers to serve on a part-time basis as school resource officers in schools in Etowah County."
"A person who retired from the position of municipal police officer, deputy sheriff... and who retired in good standing may be employed as a part-time school resource officer by Etowah County..."
